name: Difficulty Settings
description: Puts back the Options dialog's Difficulty choice -- Easy, Normal or Hard -- as A New Home, The Lost Children and The Secret City have it. New Believers already plays by a difficulty level, saved with each village (a village starts on Normal), and its rules are The Secret City's, but its Options dialog never shows the choice. With this patch the Difficulty row is drawn where The Secret City has it, directly above Game Speed, with the game's own radio buttons, words and font; Game Speed moves down a row and the dialog's frame grows by whole tiles, so the whole dialog stays on the screen with everything in it where it was. The choice is saved with the village. The Done button sits 20 pixels higher than in the stock dialog, clear of the frame's bottom bar as in The Tree of Life (not yet checked in a live game). Easy: a new village starts with 300 more food; villagers never eat the extra food the other levels take; a fed, healthy villager tries to regain health on every check instead of about half of them; and villagers fall sick about a quarter as often. Normal (a village's level until you change it): above 8,000 food each villager's meal takes 2 more food three times in four; a starving villager loses health on about three checks in four. Hard: a new village starts with 99 less food; each villager's meal takes 2 more food three times in four at any food level; a starving villager loses health on every check. **The starting food only changes for a village made after you pick the level; the other rules follow the level at once.** **Needs no other patch; it works the same with every other patch and in every population mode.** **Checked in a live game, windowed: the row's layout, every button, and the chosen level after a save and reload. Clicks in fullscreen have not been tried in a live game.** It is on by default; untick it to keep the stock dialog (a village then keeps the level it has). The companion is "VVFP Difficulty.dll", started by VVFP Startup.dll; if the DLL cannot be loaded, the stock dialog is shown.
behavior_changes: The Options dialog (drawing 0x41ADF0, clicks 0x41B5C0) shows a Difficulty row at y+0x161: the heading and three radio buttons with Easy, Normal and Hard (strings 0x57E Difficulty, 0x57F Easy, 0x584 Normal (Game Speed's own), 0x581 Hard), the selected one the village's level (game-state field +0x17D54).

Game Speed's buttons, heading, labels and click areas move down 0x64 (100 pixels, the dialog's own spacing between its Fullscreen and Game Speed rows), to y+0x1C5; the dialog's height becomes 0x27C, so its frame is two 64-pixel tiles taller (640 pixels on the 1024 x 768 screen); the frame, the Done button and the Music Tracks checkboxes are placed by the game from the frame, and the rows from the frame's top + 2 as in the stock dialog, so nothing else moves against them.

The stock handler's own three Difficulty click areas (0x41B9B9 / 0x41B9E7 / 0x41BA19 write 0, 1, 2) move onto the new row's buttons, with the Game Speed buttons' insets; no click near Game Speed changes the level any more.

The level's effects are the stock game's own (starting food 0x4248EB; food use, starvation and healing 0x472DBB..0x472F81; sickness 0x472F81 and 0x465F58): Easy: a new village starts with 300 more food; villagers never eat the extra food the other levels take; a fed, healthy villager tries to regain health on every check instead of about half of them; and villagers fall sick about a quarter as often. Normal (a village's level until you change it): above 8,000 food each villager's meal takes 2 more food three times in four; a starving villager loses health on about three checks in four. Hard: a new village starts with 99 less food; each villager's meal takes 2 more food three times in four at any food level; a starving villager loses health on every check.
explicit_non_changes: This row changes no executable bytes: VVFP Difficulty.dll verifies every stock byte it rewrites and writes them at run time; a different build of the game installs nothing.
No save byte, file or villager is written by the companion: the level is the stock field, written only by the game's own click handler and saved by the game's own save.
What each level does is unchanged: these are the stock rules, which already run on Normal in every village.
Every other row of the dialog (sound, music, voiceovers, music tracks, fullscreen) is drawn and clicked exactly as before.
